actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Capture a local acquisition timestamp when the source produces the payload, retain it in Job, and pass it to ArtifactStore::acquire for template expansion. If native adapters expose the exact capture instant, carry that timestamp with their result; otherwise source-completion time is a defensible default. Add a test that blocks an earlier upload, acquires a screenshot across a known clock boundary, then drains the queue and verifies its name retains the acquired timestamp and remains fixed on retry.
actionable_findings.title: Freeze filename time before waiting in the processing queue
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: The timestamp is sampled when the disk-acquisition worker finally runs, after the source has already captured or imported its payload. With the default concurrentUploads=1, a slow existing upload holds that worker slot while a new screenshot is acquired and queued. A screenshot acquired at 04:27:21 but processed at 04:29:00 is therefore saved and uploaded as Screen-Capture-...-04-29-00.png. That makes the new filename timestamp describe queue-drain time instead of the local acquisition time required by R29; an arbitrary upload delay changes the name of already acquired content.

actionable_findings.why_it_matters: Every fresh configuration now contains four filename-template properties and pendingImageBytes, but the published configuration schema rejects additional properties in both naming and limits and still permits only generated/original naming modes. Consequently, a configuration saved successfully by this GUI fails the schema linked from docs/configuration.md, and schema-guided editors or external configuration tooling cannot validate the new default or template mode. This is newly introduced by the changed defaults and validator, rather than an unrelated defect in the unchanged schema.

actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the active deletion ID separate from selected-row display state, or prevent selectionChanged from replacing it while deletionTimer_ is active. Preserve detail/preview reloads and hidden-image release. If the timer is read during constructor-triggered selectionChanged, initialize its pointer to nullptr before construction and guard that access. Add a delayed synthetic-deletion test that confirms the exact prepared target, hides/shows History before row refresh, clicks Cancel deletion, and asserts that the active deletion receives cancellation and remains inspectable.
actionable_findings.title: Preserve active deletion cancellation when History reopens
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: After the user confirms a deletion, prepareDelete retains its live operation ID and starts polling. If History is hidden and reopened while that deletion remains active, the newly added showEvent calls selectionChanged, which replaces the live ID with the cached selected row value. That value can still be empty or stale because deletion acceptance does not refresh the row. Cancel deletion then returns immediately or targets the obsolete ID, so pending destructive work receives no cancellation request; progress polling and its final refresh can also stop. The frozen source independently proves this state transition, and the caller supplies a deterministic before-fix widget failure for the hide/show plus Cancel trigger.
actionable_findings.validation_reason: When an accepted deletion remains active and its selected cached row has an empty or stale deleteOperationId, the newly added HistoryWindow.cpp:86–88 showEvent invokes selectionChanged at :57 and overwrites the live ID without refreshing the model, causing Cancel at :53 to return or target the obsolete operation and polling at :91 to lose the active operation; HistoryService.cpp:45,82,89 provides no compensating refresh or cancellation lookup, and the supplied pre-fix Qt 6.4.2 offscreen Debug reproduction exercises confirmation, hide/show, detail completion and Cancel and fails the Cancellation requested assertion, establishing synthetic widget incidence without desktop or real-storage acceptance.

advisoryBoundaries.title: Original-name preservation excludes valid Linux filenames
advisoryBoundaries.why_it_matters: Imported basenames containing backslashes or control characters now cause filename_invalid and abort the complete acquisition batch. This restriction is intentional in the new test, but its effect on existing Linux-file imports and the advertised preservation rule has not been measured. Review that boundary before advertising unrestricted basename preservation.
